thread.title: Special Participation B: Deepeseek on HW 12
thread.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>For this special participation, I tested <bold>Deepseek</bold> on the coding portion question 4: Variational Autoencoders from Homework 12. I began by explaining the problem setup and topic at hand, asking Deepseek to acknowledge its understanding, after which I provided the actual code which needed to be completed. I found Deepseek to be quite capable of solving the coding problems with minimal intervention from my part.</paragraph><paragraph>Where Deepseek struggled was in identifying the functions in the imported python packages and how to use them. Since the functions in these packages were not explicitly given in the code, it seems Deepseek chose to avoid using them as much as possible. After first prompting the code to use the specified function, and correcting the LLM to output the mean and not the distributions, Deepseek was eventually able to arrive at the correct answer. </paragraph><paragraph>Overall, I found that Deepseek is perfectly able to complete multi-step coding tasks, especially in deep thinking mode, but it struggles to make connections to code not explicitly listed in the input. It seems to require a bit of goading to actually use imported functions, and may not get them right the first time. Thus it might be better to explicitly include all the functions one might want to use in the context window when coding with Deepseek.</paragraph><paragraph><link href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vZUJPw6LZF3rBgcZaoimjIf5LkLpG8sT/view?usp=sharing"><underline>Here is the link to my annotated LLM trace of the conversation</underline></link></paragraph></document>
thread.document:
For this special participation, I tested Deepseek on the coding portion question 4: Variational Autoencoders from Homework 12. I began by explaining the problem setup and topic at hand, asking Deepseek to acknowledge its understanding, after which I provided the actual code which needed to be completed. I found Deepseek to be quite capable of solving the coding problems with minimal intervention from my part.

Where Deepseek struggled was in identifying the functions in the imported python packages and how to use them. Since the functions in these packages were not explicitly given in the code, it seems Deepseek chose to avoid using them as much as possible. After first prompting the code to use the specified function, and correcting the LLM to output the mean and not the distributions, Deepseek was eventually able to arrive at the correct answer. 

Overall, I found that Deepseek is perfectly able to complete multi-step coding tasks, especially in deep thinking mode, but it struggles to make connections to code not explicitly listed in the input. It seems to require a bit of goading to actually use imported functions, and may not get them right the first time. Thus it might be better to explicitly include all the functions one might want to use in the context window when coding with Deepseek.
